title: Controlled Real Greeting — activity cover
note:
Cover, and the composition constraint is measured rather than guessed. The previous cover lost the guest's head to the 16:7 Today band, which is an acceptable trade for a step image and not for a cover. Three figures have to sit inside both the band and the centred square, and every cover that passed first time has a crouching or kneeling human — so the guest crouches.

The crop instruction was rewritten from a safe area to a drawn size before the first restyle round, the same change made to door-place-cover. Stating a safe area has now failed on four scenes; restating it as a size plus an empty margin landed first try on three of them. The leash clip was also added to mustBeTrue: two pictures this session — round 33 of door-sound-05-settle and round 47 of door-greet-09-leaves — came back with the leash hanging from a hand attached to nothing, and both had review questions that asked only about slackness.
scene: Interior entry hall, the open front door behind the figures with pale daylight and flat spruce foliage beyond it. Lucy SITS at the handler's side with all four paws on the floor, calm and square, on a black leash that hangs from her collar ring in a visibly slack curve to the handler's hand. The handler stands close beside her. The guest is a step away, CROUCHED down on his heels so his head comes to about Lucy's height, hands resting on his own knees and at his sides — he is not reaching for her and not touching her. The guest wears the medium-blue zip-up hoodie, black baseball cap and clear-framed glasses from his likeness reference. He is NOT in a plaid or checked shirt — that was an earlier version of this character and is being replaced everywhere. HOW BIG THE GROUP IS DRAWN: draw all three SMALLER than the composition wants, grouped close together near the middle rather than spread across the frame. The top of the standing handler's head — the highest thing in the picture — sits about a QUARTER of the way down from the top edge and no higher; the lowest thing that matters, Lucy's paws and the guest's feet, no lower than three quarters of the way down. Above every head leave a clear band of empty lavender wall at least a fifth of the picture's height with nothing in it, and below them clear empty floor. Left and right, nothing that matters enters the outer eighth of the width. The app crops this two ways at once — a wide Today band keeping only the middle strip of the HEIGHT, and a centred square keeping only the middle three-quarters of the WIDTH — so a head near the top edge is decapitated on the app's largest surface. Empty wall above them is better than a sliced head.
mustBeTrue: the top of the handler's head sits about a quarter of the way down the frame with a clear band of empty wall above every head, and nothing that matters falls in the top fifth, the bottom quarter or the outer eighth of either side — so neither the Today band nor the centred square cuts a head; the guest is crouched down on his heels rather than standing over her, he is not reaching for or touching her, and Lucy sits with all four paws on the floor on a leash that is visibly clipped to her collar ring and slack.
